items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That was a tough school, but it changed my life, along with Fran Sweeney.

ctx.x: How did your family react to your interest in the music of . . .?

My father, who was on the road most of the time, just thought that was part of my obsessiveness. I used to have so many books that the books crowded into the living room, which he didn’t much like. My mother couldn’t understand why I was playing that stuff. She said, “It all sounds the same.” It almost drove her crazy. When Fran Sweeney died, I kept playing Ben Webster ballads again and again and again. As I said, it was an essential part of my life.

The way you’re talking about the books and the obsessiveness and everything, it brings up the Talmud to me. I think of you almost as a Talmudic scholar related to what it is that you do. Was the Talmud and that kind of study – was that something that you observed people doing at the . . .?
